newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FORECAST - Singapore Oct exports seen down 1.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Singapore Oct exports seen down 1.4 pct.

text.p: Singapore's exports have begun to recover from the recent slump in global electronics demand, a Reuters poll of economists suggested on Tuesday.
Fifteen financial institutions produced an average forecast of a fall of 1.4 percent year-on-year in nominal terms in the city-state's non-oil domestic exports in October.
This would be a bounce back from the 6.2 percent fall registered in September and a decline of 6.3 percent in August.
But there was no consensus on the scale of the improvement.
Of the 15 economists polled, only three came up with an identical figure -- a fall of two percent -- and estimates ranged from a fall of 5.3 percent to a rise of three percent.
The Trade Development Board is expected to publish the country's official export figures for October on November 20.
Singapore's exports have suffered over the last six months as a result of a slump in the electronics industry in the United States and Japan.
Electronics, computers and related products account for about half the island's total industrial production and almost 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
This dependence helped pull down Singapore's economic growth to a year-on-year rise of just 3.2 percent in the third quarter, from 11.4 percent in the first three months of the year.
Economists say there are now signs of a small recovery in the U.S. electronics industry which may be beginning to filter through to stronger demand for Singapore exports.
But this evidence is mostly anecdotal and they say it will probably take another six months before exports, and therefore economic growth, begin to rebound strongly.

The same Reuters poll forecast a rise of 1.5 percent year-on-year in Singapore's consumer price index (CPI) of inflation in October. The index rose 1.5 percent year-on-year in September and by 1.4 percent in August.
